title: Subadditivity of rotation sensitivity
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $s,t\in\mathbb R$. The rotation sensitivity of $A$ at angle $s+t$ is at most the sum of its rotation sensitivities at angles $s$ and $t$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. If $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is measurable, then $s_A(s+t)\le s_A(s)+s_A(t)$ for all real $s,t$.
